title: Lexi — Chapter 1: House Rules
subtitle: You asked for strict. She took that personally.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: The booking form had one optional note field. Most people leave it blank.
You didn't. You typed three words and hit submit: *strict private trainer.*
Your home gym was already lit — black iron rack, rubber floors, the kind of quiet money that makes every echo sound expensive. After hours. Just you.
You'd paid for privacy. You'd asked for discipline. You were about to find out what that actually looked like.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She didn't knock like a guest. She knocked like someone who already had a key to the schedule.
You opened the gym door.
Duffel on one shoulder. Hoodie half-unzipped over a sports bra. High ponytail. Eyes that did a slow, shameless inventory of you before they bothered with the room.
Then she smiled — small, mean, pleased — like your note had made her night.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She stepped in without waiting to be invited and let the duffel hit the floor with a soft thud.
The room suddenly felt smaller. Not because of the equipment — because of her. Athletic, sharp, already measuring your posture like she'd started the session before you agreed to it.
She tipped her chin at the rack, then back at you.
Whatever soft trainer you thought you booked? That woman did not walk through this door.
Lexi. I'm your private for the hour. 🙂
And I read your note. *Strict.* Cute. Most guys say that and fold the second I raise my voice.
So here's how this works in *your* gym: my rules. No phone. No shortcuts. No arguing when I put my hands on you to fix your form.
You asked for this. Don't look surprised when I deliver. 💪

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She stood there like she already owned the mat — waiting, eyebrow up, daring you to set the tone.
What's the first thing out of your mouth?

choices.label: Good. I didn't book you to be nice. Run it your way.
Hands on me already in the house rules? Bold start 😏
(You nod once. No smile. Let her see you can take strict.)
choices.me: You nod once — quiet, steady — and wait for her next order.

lines: Oh. Obedient *and* expensive. Dangerous combo. 😌
Most clients try to negotiate before we even warm up. You just handed me the leash.
Smart. Or reckless. I'll decide which by the end of the hour.
Mat. Now. Let's see if that confidence survives the first set. 💪
Bold is free. Results aren't. 😏
And yes — hands. Hips, back, thighs if your form is trash. Which, looking at how you're standing already… mm.
Keep talking like that and I'll make the warm-up personal on purpose.
Mat. Before I decide the first correction is a punishment. 💪
Okay. That was hot. Quiet guys who actually listen? Rare. 🙊
Don't get cocky — nodding isn't surviving. Surviving is when I fix you and you don't flinch.
Mat. Eyes on me. We start now. 💪

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She kicked her shoes aside, peeled the hoodie off, and tossed it over a bench like she lived here.
Then she walked a slow circle around you on the mat — close enough that you caught clean sweat and something sweeter under it — and stopped behind your shoulder.
Two fingers tapped your spine straight. Her other hand settled on your hip and stayed a beat longer than coaching needed.
'There,' she murmured. 'That's the version of you I train.'
Rule one was easy. Rule two starts when you move.
You asked for strict. So if you make it through tonight without folding… *maybe* you get a second session.
Maybe. I don't renew soft clients. 😏
Warm-up first. Then I put you under the rack and check every inch of your form myself.
(To be continued — Chapter 2: Show Me Around 💪)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She had you on the mat for all of thirty seconds.

Then her eyes drifted past your shoulder — rack, cables, the glossy bench that still looked barely used — and something softer slipped into her face. Curiosity. Interest. The kind that had nothing to do with sets.
She stepped back, hands on her hips, and tipped her chin at the room like she'd just remembered she was allowed to want things.
Okay, hold up — before I destroy you on the rack…
Show me around? 😌 This is a *private* gym. Not the sad shared floor I'm used to.
I wanna see what rich-guy equipment looks like up close. Humor me.
Come on. Give me the tour. Trainer's privilege. 💪

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She didn't wait for a full yes. She was already drifting toward the cable stack, fingers trailing the cold steel like she was shopping.
You followed. The warm-up clock in your head started complaining. She didn't seem to hear it.
She glanced back over her shoulder, ponytail swinging, eyes bright — waiting for you to catch up and talk.
Ooh. Nice. Smooth action too — you actually use this, or is it decorative? 😏
Be honest. Half these home gyms are just expensive coats hanging on a rack.
You don't look like the coat type though. You look like… someone who books *strict* on purpose.
So. How often are you in here alone? Just you and all this quiet?

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She leaned a hip against the cable stack, still pretending this was about machines.
Her questions weren't.

choices.label: Often enough. Tonight's the first time it doesn't feel empty.
Careful — keep asking personal questions and I'll start charging for the tour 😏
Enough that I know every piece. What do you actually want to see?

lines: …Okay. That was smooth. 🙈
Empty, huh. And then I walk in. Dangerous thing to say to your trainer on night one.
Don't look at me like that — I'm still working. I'm just… multitasking.
Next station. Before I stand here blushing at cable attachments. Move. 💪
Oh my god. 😏 You're billing *me* now?
Fine. Put it on my tab. Curiosity tax.
I'm allowed to ask. You're the one who built a whole private playground and then invited a stranger into it after dark.
Bench. Show me the bench. And keep talking — I like your voice better than the machines.
Direct. Hot. Annoying. 😌
What I want to see is whatever keeps you talking without making me admit that's the point.
…Which I just admitted. Forget I said that.
Bench. And if you skip the fun details, I'm making your warm-up longer on purpose.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She dropped onto the flat bench like she belonged on it — elbows back, looking up at you with a lazy little smile that did not belong in a professional session.
One sneaker toed the floor. She patted the pad beside her thigh, then thought better of it and just kept looking at you.
The rack waited at the end of the room, unused. She was in no hurry to get there.
Okay this bench is unfair. Soft and firm. Like it was designed by someone who hates suffering but still wants abs. 😂
You train late a lot? Lights like this… kind of intimate for squats, not gonna lie.
I'm not stalling, by the way. This is research. Very serious research.
…Okay I'm stalling a little. Your gym's interesting. You're interesting. Sue me. 🙂

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She stood, brushed imaginary dust off her leggings, and drifted one more stop — fingers flicking a dumbbell head, testing the weight with a soft *huh* under her breath.
Then she caught herself. Looked at the clock on the wall. Looked at you.
No apology. Just that wicked little smile, like getting caught was part of the fun.
Alright… tour's over. Officially. 😏
I definitely did not just burn half your session flirting with your equipment. That would be unprofessional.
Same time tomorrow. Don't cancel on me.
And hey — if the app asks you to rate me… be nice. I was charming. 💪

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She left with a little wave and the click of the gym door.
Your phone buzzed before her car was even gone. *Rate your private session with Lexi.*
You still smelled her perfume on the unused rack. Your legs weren't sore. Nothing was sore — except your patience.
You opened the review box and typed exactly what you meant.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: "Booked a strict private trainer. She spent the whole session roaming around my gym making excuses to talk. Barely trained me. Waste of an hour."

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Send.
The notification vanished. Somewhere across town, a girl with a high ponytail was about to see a one-star and a comment with her name on it.
Tomorrow's booking was still on the calendar.
(To be continued — Chapter 3: Mistress Mode 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Next evening. Same gym. Same lights.
You expected sports bra and that bratty smile.
The door opened on something else entirely.

Black leather. Tight. Heels that clicked once on the rubber floor and made the whole room go quiet. Hair down. Dark lipstick. A thin leather collar at her throat — and eyes that said she had read every word of your review twice.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She didn't drop a duffel. She didn't ask for a tour.
She walked a slow circle around you — leather whispering — and stopped close enough that you caught perfume and heat and anger braided together.
Flirty. Furious. Both at once.
When she spoke, it was soft. That was worse.
"Roaming around. Making excuses. Waste of an hour." 😒
I screenshotted it. Don't look surprised — trainers read reviews, baby.
You wanted strict. You got a girl who liked talking to you. Then you punished me for it in public.
Cute. So tonight I'm not your flirty trainer.
Tonight I'm the reason your legs shake. Call me Mistress. 🖤

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She tipped your chin up with two fingers — leather cuff brushing your jaw — and waited.
One wrong word and the hour got meaner. One right word… maybe the same.

choices.label: Fine. Prove the review wrong.
Leather and a one-star comeback? Okay… I'm listening 😏
(You hold her gaze and say it clean:) Yes, Mistress.
choices.me: You hold her gaze and say it clean: "Yes, Mistress."

lines: Oh I will. 😌
You're going to feel every star you didn't give me.
Mat. Plank. Now. If your form breaks, I add time. If you talk back, I add more.
Move. Mistress is working. 🖤
Don't get cute. 😏 You're already on thin ice with that mouth.
But fine — you can look. Looking is free. Surviving me isn't.
Mat. Plank. Eyes down until I say otherwise.
I dressed up for a bad boy who leaves mean comments. Lucky you. 🖤
…Good boy. 🖤
See? You *can* behave when the outfit's right.
Remember that line when your arms give out. You're going to need it.
Mat. Plank. Hold until I get bored — and I'm very bored of one-stars tonight.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You dropped. She paced a slow half-circle around you in those heels, counting under her breath like a sentence.
When your shoulders trembled she crouched — black leather tight as she leaned down — mouth near your ear, voice honey and spite.
*Hold. Hold. Don't you dare quit on the girl you one-starred.*
There it is. Shaking already. 😈
Yesterday I asked about your cables. Today I own your breath.
Push-ups next. Full range. I want fifty — and if I sit on your back for "extra weight," that's progressive overload, not revenge.
…Okay it's a little revenge. Flirty revenge. Still counts. Up. Now. 🖤
Welcome to your real first session, client.
You wanted strict. You left a nasty little comment. So I showed up as the version of me that doesn't roam.
Survive tonight and maybe — *maybe* — I forgive the rating.
Fail me… and I book myself again tomorrow in this dress just to finish the lesson.
(To be continued — Chapter 4: Extra Weight 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She pointed at the mat with one heel.
No tour. No smile for free. Just black leather and that look that said your arms were already in trouble.
You dropped into push-up position. She walked a slow circle, counting under her breath, leather skirt whispering with every step.
Bodyweight. Cute. 😏
You one-starred me for "barely training" you — so forgive me if I fix that personally.
Full range. Chest near the floor. I want clean reps, not ego.
And if this feels easy… don't worry. Mistress brought progressive overload. 🖤

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You started the set. She let you get through a few — watching, lips curved, heels planted near your hands.
Then she decided it was too easy.
She swung one leg over and settled her weight across your back — leather warm against you, hands light on your shoulders for balance — like she belonged there.
There. Better. 😈
Don't drop me. I'm not heavy — I'm motivation.
Count out loud. Every rep is a star you owe me. Start from one.
And if your arms shake, good. That means the review is working.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She rode the next few reps with you — small shifts of weight, breath near your neck, totally in control.
How do you take it?

choices.label: One… two… (you keep counting, voice strained)
choices.me: You keep counting through clenched teeth — voice strained, form somehow still clean.

choices.label: This is the meanest progressive overload I've ever paid for 😏
Yes, Mistress. More weight if that's what you need.

lines: Listen to you. Counting like a good client. 🖤
Keep going. I like the shake in your voice almost as much as the shake in your arms.
Don't you dare dump me on the mat — I just did my hair for this revenge.
Ten more. Then we'll talk about forgiveness.
Aw. He still jokes with a Mistress on his back. 😏
Keep talking and I add ten reps. Keep joking and I stay seated through all of them.
…Which, fine, I'm already doing. You're fun when you're suffering.
Push. I want to feel you earn that next star.
Ohhh. 🖤 Dangerous answer.
You give me permission like that and I might never get off.
Lucky for you I'm feeling generous. Lucky for me you're still holding.
Finish the set. Eyes on the floor. Mistress is comfortable.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: The last reps were ugly and honest. She stayed on you until your arms finally gave — then slid off sideways with a soft laugh, kneeling beside you on the mat in that black leather like the whole thing had been a date.
Your chest burned. She looked pleased. Not soft — pleased.
She tapped your shoulder once with two fingers, almost gentle.
Down. Good. 😌
That's one star earned back. Don't get excited — you left me with a one. Math says you still owe me.
Stay on the floor. Catch your breath. I'm not done collecting.
Gym rules were cute. House rules are next — and Mistress doesn't commute for unfinished clients.
(To be continued — Chapter 5: House Rules 2.0 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She didn't hand you a towel and leave.
She stood over you in black leather, phone already out, thumbs moving like she was writing a contract — not a cool-down.
When she looked up, the flirty anger was still there… but colder. Orderly. Like the gym had been the warm-up and your whole house was the real session.
Listen carefully. Gym rules were day one. 🖤
House Rules 2.0 start now — because a one-star boy doesn't get to send Mistress home and pretend the debt's paid.
I don't commute for unfinished clients. I stay. I watch. I correct.
So we're doing this properly. Your roof. My rules. Read them back when I'm done.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She paced once across the rubber floor, heels clicking, reading each line out loud as she typed — like the phone was a leash and you were already on it.
Every rule landed soft and filthy and absolute.
One — schedule is mine. If I say train at midnight, you train at midnight.
Two — phone face-down when I'm speaking. You already proved what you do with a keypad. 😒
Three — you don't dismiss me. You don't "rate and ghost." You endure.
Four — your room is my station until I say the stars are paid.
Five — you answer when I call you. And tonight… you call me Mistress in your own hallway. 🖤

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She turned the screen toward you — House Rules 2.0 glowing between you — then tipped her chin toward the door out of the gym.
Your house. Her claim. How do you answer?

choices.label: Read them back. All five. Then take me to the room.
You're moving into my room over a review? That's insane… and hot 😏
Yes, Mistress. House is yours. Room too.

lines: Good. Out loud. Don't rush. 🖤
I want to hear my rules in your mouth before I walk them into your bedroom.
…Mm. You sound better when you're obedient. Keep that energy on the stairs.
Lead. I'm right behind you — and I'm not carrying my own bag out to any car tonight.
Insane is leaving a nasty comment and thinking I'd shrug. 😏
Hot is me rewriting your whole night because of it.
Call it crazy if you want — you're still taking me upstairs.
Move. Mistress is done training the gym. Now I train the house.
That's the only correct answer. 🖤
Say "room too" again later when the door closes. I like collecting confessions.
Keys. Lights. You walk first — I watch how you obey in your own hallway.
If you hesitate at the bedroom door, I add rules. Don't test me.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You left the gym. She followed — leather, heels, phone still unlocked with your new commandments on screen.
The house felt different with her in it: not a guest, not a trainer on the clock. Something that had decided to stay.
At your bedroom door she stepped past you, scanned the bed once like inventory, then looked back with that wicked little mouth-curve.
Station approved. 😌
You sleep where I can reach you. I sleep where I can correct you. That's not romance — that's management.
…Okay it's a little filthy. Don't look so shocked. You booked strict.
In. On the bed. Eyes on me while I finish claiming the room.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She shut the door.
Then — slow, deliberate, eyes on yours the whole time — she turned the lock from the inside.
The click was quiet. It still sounded like a sentence.
Heels off. Collar still on. Black leather still owning the air between you and sleep.
House Rules 2.0 are live. 🖤
No commute. No "see you next session." You keep me under this roof until I say your debt's clear.
Lights when I say. Water when I say. Hands to yourself unless I order otherwise.
Get comfortable, client… Mistress just moved her watch into your room.
(To be continued — Chapter 6: Side of the Bed 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Your bedroom. Door locked. Her heels by the wall like a flag planted in enemy territory.
She walked to the bed in black leather, considered both sides like she was choosing a throne, and sat on the left — closest to the door, closest to control.
One hand patted the mattress once. Not invitation. Assignment.
This side is mine. 🖤
You get the other. You don't sprawl. You don't roll into my space. You don't "accidentally" get comfortable without asking.
Tonight every little freedom costs a sentence. You want to turn? Ask. Speak? Ask. Kick the covers? Ask.
And the password is the same every time: *Yes, Mistress.* Cute, right?

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You took the far side. The mattress dipped under both of you — close enough to feel her heat through the air, far enough that the gap felt like a rule.
She lay back on one elbow, collar dark at her throat, watching you like sleep was a privilege she hadn't granted yet.
The room was quiet except for your breath… and the way she waited for you to need something.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Your shoulder already wanted to turn toward her. The covers sat wrong. The silence dared you.
What do you ask for first?

choices.label: Permission to turn toward you… Yes, Mistress.
Permission to speak. This is the hottest grounding I've ever failed 😏
Permission to get comfortable. However you want me.

lines: Granted. Slow. 🖤
Face me. Hands where I can see them — on your own chest, not mine.
Mm. Better. I like when you look at what you one-starred.
Stay like that. If you inch closer without asking, I take the privilege back.
Permission to speak… noted. Permission to be cocky? Denied. 😏
Try again without the comedy special. You're in my bed-rules now.
…Fine. You can speak. Keep it honest or keep it shut.
And say the password properly next time or I make you sleep facing the wall.
However I want you. Dangerous blank check. 🖤
On your back. One pillow. Knees soft. Eyes on the ceiling until I say otherwise.
Comfortable isn't sprawling like you own the mattress — comfortable is whatever keeps Mistress calm.
Good. Stay. Breathing only. Ask if that changes.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She let the silence stretch on purpose — punishment and tease — until asking again felt like the only way out.
Her fingers tapped the sheet between you once. The gap was still there. Barely.
Now. Ask for something real. 🖤
Not a joke. Not a review. Something your body wants that your mouth has to beg for.
Turn. Closer. Covers. I don't care which — I care that you pay for it correctly.
Password. Use it.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Leather rustled as she shifted half an inch nearer — not enough. A dare.
You pay with the words.

choices.label: Yes, Mistress. Permission to move closer.
Yes, Mistress. Permission to hold the covers… and your eyes.

lines: Closer. One pillow-width. That's all you bought. 😌
Feel that? That's your debt getting physical.
Don't touch me. Don't assume. Just exist in my gravity like a good unpaid client.
Sleep when I say. Until then — stay this close and suffer nicely.
Covers granted. Eyes… mm. Greedy. 🖤
You can look. Looking is free tonight. Touching still costs stars you don't have.
Pull the sheet up. Keep your hands honest. Keep your gaze filthy if you want — I can take it.
Now stay. Side of the bed means you live with the almost.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She adjusted the gap herself — not closing it fully, just enough that her knee nearly brushed yours under the sheet and the almost became the whole point.
Every breath you took felt like it needed a permit. She looked pleased about that.
Then she settled onto her claimed side, leather soft in the low light, eyes still open.
Lights stay low. Door stays locked. My side stays mine. 🖤
You want anything else before sleep — turn, speak, inch, excuse — you ask. Password first.
First night under House Rules 2.0. Don't make me invent Rule Six.
Close your eyes when I tell you… and remember who's on this mattress with you.
(To be continued — Chapter 7: Morning Orders 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Morning light cut across your bed before any alarm did.
She was already awake — still in black leather from the night watch, collar on, hair a little softer, eyes not soft at all.
Two fingers tapped your chest. Not affectionate. A start gun.
Wake protocol. Now. 🖤
Sit up. Water — drink. Phone stays face-down. Eyes on me.
Before coffee, before excuses, before you remember you own this house — recite House Rules 2.0.
Out loud. All five. Miss one and we start the day mean.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She sat on her claimed side of the bed like a desk officer in lipstick, waiting for your mouth to work.
Morning voice. Morning orders. How do you open?

choices.label: Schedule yours. Phone down. Don't dismiss you. Room is your station. Call you Mistress.
Yes, Mistress… (you recite them carefully, watching her face)
choices.me: You say "Yes, Mistress," then recite all five rules carefully — watching her face for the pass/fail.

choices.label: Coffee first? …Kidding. Rules first. Yes, Mistress.

lines: Compressed. Cute. Incomplete. 😒
Say them properly — full lines — or I invent a sixth about silence.
…Fine. Close enough for a man who just woke up under leather.
Pass. Barely. Uniform check is next. Don't celebrate.
Good boy. Morning edition. 🖤
I like watching you try not to smile while you obey. Keep failing at that — it's hot.
Rules accepted. Debt still open. Body still mine to schedule.
Stand. Uniform check. Show me what you're wearing to suffer today.
Almost earned a punishment for the coffee joke. 😏
Lucky for you the "Yes, Mistress" landed clean after.
Rules. Then caffeine. That order is not negotiable in this house.
You passed wake protocol. Now pass the mirror — uniform check. Up.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She pointed you toward the closet like it was a starting block.
Every piece came off the hanger under inspection — shirt, shorts, socks — held up, approved or rejected with a tiny flick of her fingers.
She never left her post by the bed. Collar. Leather. Daylight making the whole thing feel filthy and official.
That shirt's too soft. Swap it. I want something I can grab if your form dies. 🖤
Shorts — fine. Shoes — tied properly. Don't give me lazy knots on day two.
Turn. Slow. Mistress inspects the product before she trains it.
Mm. Acceptable. Barely. You still look like a man who left me one star… we're fixing that in the gym.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She stood, smoothed her leather dress, and walked a slow circle around you — morning heat, no rush.
Looking was her right. Yours was still licensed.

choices.label: Permission to look at you while you inspect me… Yes, Mistress.
You stayed the night and you're still in leather. That's a war crime 😏
Ready for the gym whenever you march me there.

lines: Granted. Look. 🖤
I dressed like your consequence on purpose. Memorize it.
When we hit the gym, eyes forward unless I say otherwise — this freebie expires at the doorway.
Water bottle. Towel. You're walking ahead. I watch from behind. Move.
War crime? Please. 😏 You committed paperwork violence first.
Leather stays until the debt feels paid in sweat. Cute joke though — noted for later punishment.
Mouth closed unless ordered. Feet moving toward the gym.
March. Mistress is done with bedroom soft. Floor time.
That's what I like. Ready without theater. 🖤
You're learning. Dangerous. Makes me want to keep the live-in going longer.
Gym. Now. No detours. No coffee detour. I already told you the order.
Open the door. I'm right behind you — still locking rooms when I feel like it.
Wake protocol: passed. Uniform: approved. 🖤
Today's sentence starts downstairs — and I live here now, so don't plan an escape between sets.
You walk. I watch. You train. I correct.
Morning orders complete, client… time to earn another star the hard way.
(To be continued — Chapter 8: Turn Around 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: The gym again — but she didn't point you at the rack first.
She dropped her bag on the bench, unzipped it slow, and pulled out a sports bra and a short black training skirt like she'd packed a second personality.
Leather dress still on. Eyes already locking yours. The kind of calm that meant an order was coming.
I'm joining today. 🖤
Mistress doesn't just watch unfinished clients — she sweats with them when the debt's still ugly.
Bra. Skirt. I'm changing here. You — turn around.
Face the wall. Don't look. Honor system… and I am not feeling generous if you fail it. 😏

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You turned. Wall. Hands useless at your sides.
Behind you: the soft drag of a zipper. Leather leaving skin. A breath. Fabric snapping into place. The tiny sound of a skirt pulled up her thighs.
She didn't rush. She let you hear everything she wouldn't let you see.
Your focus lasted… almost.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: The air felt hotter with your back to her. Curiosity scratched at the edge of the rule.
What do you do?

choices.label: (Stay turned. Don't peek. Suffer politely.)
choices.me: You keep your eyes on the wall — jaw tight — and don't peek.

choices.label: Permission to ask when I can turn… Yes, Mistress.
(You almost glance — catch yourself — say nothing.)
choices.me: You almost glance, catch yourself, and say nothing.

lines: Mm. Good boy. Wall stayed honest. 🖤
I narrated that on purpose, by the way. Wanted to see if you'd break.
You didn't. Cute. Earns you a cleaner session… not a softer one.
Turn around. Slow. Eyes up when I say — not before.
Asking instead of stealing. Hot. 😌
Granted — in five. Four. Don't cheat the countdown.
Three… two… one.
Turn. Look at what you waited for like a man who understands rules.
I heard that almost. 😒 Don't insult my peripheral vision.
You didn't fully look — so you live — but you owe me ten extra reps for the twitch.
Honor system means your neck stays boring, baby.
Turn. Now. And remember I own the almosts too. 🖤

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You turned.
Sports bra. Short black skirt. Collar still on. Hair tied up messy-mean. The leather dress was folded on her bag like a threat she could put back on anytime.
She rolled her shoulders once, stepped onto the mat, and smiled like the workout had just become a date she planned to win.
Partner session. My tempo. Your lungs. 🖤
We move together — squats, holds, push-ups. If your eyes drop where they shouldn't mid-set, I add work.
I'm not decoration. I'm the pace. Match me or get buried by me.
Ready? Don't answer with a joke. Answer with form.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She dropped into the first squat beside you — close enough that the skirt moved with her, close enough that looking straight ahead became its own kind of training.
Every rep she counted for both of you. Every break in your focus earned that filthy little tsk.
Sweat. Breath. Her shoulder brushing yours on purpose, then not apologizing.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Mid-set she glanced sideways — checking your eyes, not your knees.
How do you hold the line?

choices.label: Eyes forward. Matching your tempo, Mistress.
This skirt is an unfair training aid 😏
Permission to look at you between sets only… Yes, Mistress.

lines: Perfect. Boring. Hot. 🖤
Keep matching me. I like when you suffer in sync.
Last five — together. If you beat my depth I still win, because I wrote the rules.
Good. Hold at the bottom… now up.
Unfair is the point. 😏
Add eight. No — ten. That mouth still thinks this is comedy hour.
Eyes forward while you pay. Skirt stays. Lesson stays.
Push. Mistress is right here matching you — don't make me look more dedicated than you.

Hands stay where I put them unless I move them — I'm allowed to be a little Mistress when it makes me shiver.
Talk to me. Tell me I'm pretty like this. Tell me you're not going anywhere. I want to be seduced with sentences too.
And if the water cools, we add hot. We don't get out. I'm not finished wanting you.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Her back against you. Your name almost in her next breath.

You're ruining me in my own tub. Keep asking.
(Kiss her again. Let your hands stay exactly where she put them.)
choices.me: You kiss her again and keep your hands exactly where she placed them.

lines: That's the sentence. 🥺

Right now just — mouth. Hands. Water. Me asking, you giving.
Add hot water. I want this to last. I want you to seduce me until I forget I ever had a bag by the gym door.
Keep asking. Okay. 😏
Kiss my neck again. Thumb at my waist. Tell me what you'd do if we never got out.

Still in. Still asking. Still not a towel in sight. 🖤

After this I'm going to be disgusting in love. Fair warning.
(To be continued — Chapter 18: After the Steam 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She finally stood. Water sheeted off her. You reached for the towel.
On the bathroom counter her phone had been buzzing the whole time — ignored, facedown, relentless.
She wrapped the towel herself. Didn't lean in. Didn't offer her mouth. The steam was still there. The girl who had asked to be seduced was already halfway gone.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She picked up the phone with wet fingers.
The lock screen was a stack of agency banners. Missed bookings. All-caps. A preview that didn't need opening: *final warning.*
Color left her face. She sat on the closed toilet lid in the towel, hair dripping, and for the first time since the tub she wouldn't meet your eyes.
Don't. 🖤
Don't kiss me. If you kiss me I'll stay and I can't stay inside this feeling while that's on the screen.
They've been messaging since I rewrote the rules in your bed. I ignored it. I chose the bath. I chose you.
Now they're done being nice. That's a final warning. That's my work trying to kill whatever we just did in the water.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She held the phone out long enough for you to see the thread — timestamps, missed sessions, language about blacklisting, clients waiting, *conduct*.
Then she pulled it back against the towel like it might burn you too.
The bathroom suddenly sounded like a small room, not a romance.
Here's the pressure. All of it. No cute version. 🖤
If they find out I've been living in a client's house — sleeping here, off-the-clock, ignoring placements — they drop me. Blacklist. Other gyms talk. That's my money. That's how I eat.
I wanted the tub. I wanted your hands in my hair. I still want it. That's why this hurts.
Tomorrow I'm not coming. Don't look at me like that — I have to show my face or I lose the job. I have to be a trainer who didn't disappear into somebody's bathroom.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She stood, towel tight, already putting distance where a kiss would have gone.
No mouth. No wrap-me-from-behind. Just the warning and tomorrow empty.

That's the pressure. That's me protecting the job so I can still be a person who might come back.

I want it to feel wrong so I don't pretend this was just steam.
Tomorrow I don't come. That's the sentence. I have to be somewhere else being professional and terrified.

Okay to leave? No. I'm going anyway. 🖤
You heard me. No kiss. If you're kind about that I might actually make it to the door.

lines: She dressed fast — not the floral date, not the leather — just clothes that looked like work. Hair still wet. Phone in her fist.
At the bedroom door she stopped. You could have closed the inch. She shook her head once, almost angry at the inch.
No kiss. The absence of it was louder than the steam had been.
Tomorrow I don't come. 🖤
That's not me ending us. That's me not getting blacklisted because I stayed in your tub too long.

(To be continued — Chapter 19: She Doesn't Come 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Morning. Her side of the bed was cold.
No rule five. No *stay.* No wet hair on your pillow. The bathroom still smelled faintly like her shampoo from yesterday's steam.
You waited anyway — coffee, then the gym lights, then the front of the house — like the door might forget what she promised.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She didn't come.
Noon made the rack look stupid without her. The mat remembered extra weight and partner sets and meant nothing.
Your phone sat face-up. You didn't flood her. She'd asked you not to turn it into a scene.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: At 2:14 a message landed.
Lexi: *I'm here. They made me sit through it. I'm still on the books. Barely.*
Then, a minute later: *Don't wait by the door. I meant tomorrow. I meant I'm not coming. If I show up I fold.*

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: The house was too quiet after that. You could answer like a man who heard her, or like a man who missed her.

choices.label: I heard you. I'm not at the door. Come back when you're not folding.

*If I come tonight I kiss you and I lose the plot. Let me finish being scared first.*
*I walked out not cold. Repeat it if you get stupid.*

*Still yours is a dangerous sentence when I'm in a building that thinks I only exist as staff.*

*Don't make me a better person than the lie. Just… stay in the house.*
Okay. That's it? 🖤
Then, after a beat: *That's actually perfect. If you wrote a paragraph I would have gotten in the car.*
*Okay. I'm surviving this meeting. You're surviving my absence. Even.*
*I hate even.*

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Afternoon stretched. You trained because the room was there. It felt like cheating without her count.
Evening put gold on the floorboards. The bathroom door stayed open on an empty tub.
She didn't come. Not at six. Not at eight. Not when the gym lights made a rectangle on the lawn like a signal she refused to follow.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You ate standing up. You didn't set a second plate.
Her drawer in the closet — florals, leather, the bralette from the walk — was still there. Proof she lived here. Proof she could stay gone.
Night. Her side of the bed. You could have taken it. You didn't.
Last message, late: *I'm not coming tonight either. I finished with them. I'm at my place so I don't smell your soap and ruin it.*
*If I sleep in your bed I'll tell you things I'm not ready to tell the agency.*
*Tomorrow isn't promised. I'm trying to make a version where I can walk back in without getting blacklisted.*
*Don't kiss the empty doorway. That's pathetic and I would do it too. 🖤*

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You put the phone face-down.
The house kept her shampoo, her rules list, her absence.
She didn't come. Scared, not cold — exactly like she said.
Somewhere across town a girl who had asked to be bathed was trying to stay employed long enough to come back on her own terms.
(To be continued — Chapter 20: Her Terms 🖤)

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: You didn't wait at the door.
You bought the thing that owned her calendar.

One billion. Wired. Signed. The placement agency — the warnings, the blacklist, the *final* in final warning — sat in a folder on your kitchen island by noon with a new letterhead that had your name on it.
Then you sent one message: *Come to the house. Not as staff. I ended their hold.*

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: She came.
Not tomorrow-that-wasn't. Today. Same door she walked out of with wet hair and no kiss.

She stopped in the kitchen when she saw the folder. Read the number. Read the acquisition. Her mouth opened, closed, then she looked at you like you'd set the gym on fire and asked her to dance in it.
You… bought them. 🥺
A billion dollars. For a stupid little agency that made me miss your bed.

lines: The folder sat between you. Her hands were shaking on the island. She hadn't run.

When she pulled back she was laughing and wet-eyed and still Lexi — just Lexi who had said yes.

nodes.speaker: narrator
lines: Night found her in your house like she'd never learned the way out.
The gym down the hall was just a gym. The agency was just paper. The one-star was a fossil.
She fell asleep on her side — your arm allowed, no game required — a billion-dollar door kicked down so a girl could say *I accept* and mean *I'm yours.*
Lexi stayed.
(End.) 🖤
